correctness.rationale: The frozen Finding incorrectly says every other off-diagonal entry is positive at either threshold. At T_(2,q), u=rho_q>rho_* and F_3(u)<0, so the distance-three entries are still strictly negative. The complete corrected RESULT.md in /workspace/repairs/1 explicitly lists both threshold signs and removes an ambiguous interval description; at T_(3,q) the other two off-diagonal shells really are positive. I rederived the distance-r entry from the coefficient of z^k in (1-z)^r(1+(q-1)z)^(3-r), weighted by u^(k²)/q³: each coordinate eigenvalue is 0 or q. For r=1, replacing the negative u⁹ term by negative u⁴ gives the stated positive lower bound, and r=0 is positive. The factored F_3 has one interior zero by strict quintic monotonicity; F_2 has exactly two simple positive zeros by Descartes, F_2(0)=1, and F_2'(1)=2q>0 at its known zero u=1. At rho_*<1/2, F_2=F_3+q(u-2u⁴+u⁹)>0, ordering the zeros. The positive row sum is exactly one, so summing negative mass over shell multiplicities gives the induced infinity norm, and symmetry gives the one-norm. Descartes and the sign near 1 give the unique interior zero sigma of 1-2u³+u⁸; F_2(sigma)=F_3(sigma)<0 and F_2 increases in q at rho_q, yielding rho_q increasing to sigma. The independent bounded replay python /workspace/reproduce_frozen.py confirms the shell and factor identities and the stated far/limit decimals. The proof, not this replay, supplies the all-q statements. Frozen numerical checker inspected, not run.
